events.description:
The purpose of this event is to kick off Mentorship Week for the Black Student Union by creating an exciting and welcoming environment for incoming freshmen and our returning students. Potential mentors and mentees will have the opportunity to mingle amongst each other while interacting with activities presented. The purpose of the first day is to break the ice and to get acquainted with each other. At the end day, potential mentees and mentors will fill out a form indicating whether they would like to continue with the program and be matched up. 

For the second event of Mentorship Week, attendees will have the chance to further meet potential mentors and mentees while doing various arts and crafts activities. Participants will step into the world of Toy Story and will be able to create their own characters inspired by the movie, highlighting important things about themselves. There will be opportunities to move around from station to station, allowing conversations to flow as pairings start to be formed. At the end of the event, participants will have a better understanding of the program and can solidify who they want to be matched up with at the end.

The purpose of the The Roundup Scavenger Hunt is to bring mentors and mentees together in a fun setting that encourages collaboration and connection. Through challenges centered on teamwork, communication, and problem-solving, mentors and mentees are given the opportunity to get to know one another on a more personal level while working toward a shared goal. Ultimately, the scavenger hunt aims to strengthen the foundation of each mentor-mentee relationship early in the program. They will be able to explore different relationships in group of 3 mentors and 3 mentees to help finalize their choice in the mentorship pair.

events.description:
Women’s Ultimate is passionate about creating an inclusive student organization that promotes and values diversity. Our commitment to inclusion across race, gender, ethnicity, religion, or any other aspects that make our members unique is what allows our club to strengthen and grow. We do not tolerate any form of discrimination and strive to incorporate diversity, equity, and inclusion practices at the center of organization.

The UF Women's Ultimate Frisbee Club Team was founded in 2001, originally as "FUEL" (Florida Ultimate Elite Ladies).

The club includes both FUEL and our B-Team, DIESEL. Any UF student is welcome to come out and play and we guarantee you'll have a great time. There is a spot for everyone! The majority of people who come out have never played before.

Both teams compete in 4-6 tournaments a year against other schools, mostly in the southeast. However, FUEL has traveled as far as California, Texas, and Colorado in the last few years for competition.

We are funded by the University, which covers the majority of our costs.

FUEL qualified for Nationals in 2006, 2007, 2011, 2012, 2017 and 2018. In their seventh year, DIESEL was the only B-team to have qualified for and played in Regionals.

Come join us for practice and see what it's all about!

The UF Women's Ultimate Frisbee Club Team was founded in 2001, originally as "FUEL" (Florida Ultimate Elite Ladies).

The club includes both FUEL and our B-Team, DIESEL. Any UF student is welcome to come out and play and we guarantee you'll have a great time. There is a spot for everyone! The majority of people who come out have never played before.
